chapter.title: Maintenance and Troubleshooting
chapter.prerequisites: Chapter 1, especially 1.6 Robot Anatomy and Coordinate Frames and 1.7 The Industrial Robot Cell; 2.5 End-of-Arm Tooling and I/O; 4.4 Making a Robot Cell Safe; 8.1 From Wires to Networks; 8.3 Lab: Connecting a Robot to a PLC. Python for the lab in 9.6.
chapter.handsOn: query a stand-in for the Universal Robots Dashboard Server over TCP port 29999 from Python to check robot mode, safety status, and program state, and recover from a protective stop; no hardware needed.
chapter.summary: Preventive, predictive, and reactive maintenance strategies and inspection intervals, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 lockout/tagout and controller log troubleshooting, mechanical cable carriers, dress packs, and joint brakes, multimeter electrical diagnostics and 24 V sensor I/O faults, axis zero-synchronization, TCP calibration, and controller storage recovery, and a Python Dashboard Server remote state monitoring lab.

lessons.title: Preventive Maintenance
objectives: Distinguish between preventive, predictive, and reactive maintenance strategies and compare their impact on machine downtime and defect rates.
Identify the maintenance intervals recommended for robot inspection, safety function testing, and service center checks.
Follow a robot maker's inspection checklist (UR's plan) for the arm, the monthly safety tests and the control box, including correct cleaning and ESD precautions.
Perform fastener and joint inspections following collisions using calibrated torque wrenches and explain the significance of joint grease.

lessons.title: A Troubleshooting Method
objectives: Follow the five-step OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 lockout/tagout sequence to isolate machinery and relieve stored hazardous energy.
Differentiate energy isolating devices from control circuit devices and evaluate lock and tag hardware specifications.
Analyze robot controller log entries, error code numbering ranges across controller generations, and flight record diagnostics.
Interpret Safety Control Board status LEDs and explain why resetting faults without root cause analysis risks component failure and injury.

lessons.title: Mechanical Problems
objectives: Apply cable routing rules for dress packs: bend radius, stress loops, cable ties and corners, and explain what cable retraction systems do.
Recognize seal wear and leakage, and state the replacement rule for flat rings and the torque for joint lid screws.
Work through UR's checklist for repeated protective stops and use backdrive mode to move an arm away from an obstacle.
Recognize a joint brake fault, explain why the arm may drop when power is removed, and check brake engagement.

lessons.title: Electrical and I/O Faults
objectives: Configure a digital multimeter for DC/AC voltage and continuity testing, observing probe jack selection and polarity conventions.
Diagnose discrete sensor wiring failures, current limitations of internal versus external 24 V supplies, and leakage current issues.
Explain how galvanic isolation through a relay and off-delay pulse stretchers prevent noise problems and missed short signals.
Troubleshoot industrial communication faults using Link/Activity LEDs, Modbus watchdog timeouts, and EtherCAT Working Counters and Lost Link Counters.

lessons.title: Calibration, Backups and Recovery
objectives: Describe when and how revolution counters are updated on an ABB robot, and how this differs from entering calibration values.
Explain why correct tool load data matters and when a 4-point or 5-point TCP method is used.
Resolve joint replacement mismatches such as error C364A1 and apply Dual Robot Calibration or Program Correction by Key Waypoints.
Perform automated and manual backups using magic files and datafs partition copies, and restore controllers from bootable images.

lessons.title: Lab: Check a Robot's State from Python
objectives: Establish a TCP socket connection to the Universal Robots Dashboard Server on port 29999 using Python.
Query robot mode, safety status, and program execution state using ASCII commands terminated with newlines.
Execute the recovery sequence for protective stops by handling safety popups and unlocking the stop.
Contrast protective stop recovery with emergency stop recovery regarding manual intervention and program restart behavior.

blurbs.9-1: Preventive, predictive and reactive maintenance strategies: inspection intervals, cleaning and ESD protection, fastener torque checks, and maintenance records.
blurbs.9-2: A systematic troubleshooting method: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 lockout/tagout, controller error logs, flight records, and avoiding masked faults.
blurbs.9-3: Mechanical fault diagnosis: cable dress packs and carriers, bend radii, seal inspection, collision recovery in backdrive mode, and joint brake engagement.
blurbs.9-4: Electrical and I/O troubleshooting: multimeter voltage and continuity checks, discrete sensor wiring, 24 V power budgets, and fieldbus diagnostics.
blurbs.9-5: Calibration, backups and recovery: axis revolution counter updates, TCP calibration, joint replacement alignment, and controller storage backups.
blurbs.9-6: Lab: querying the Universal Robots Dashboard Server over TCP port 29999 with Python to check robot mode, safety status, and recover from protective stops.

glossary.backdrive mode: An operating mode that releases joint brakes where needed so the arm can be manually moved to a safe position before initializing.
glossary.brake solenoid: An electromechanical actuator that technicians replace first before investigating the friction brake when repairing a faulty joint brake.
glossary.cable carrier: A cable guidance mechanism featuring a fixed bending radius stop to prevent cable stress.
glossary.cable retraction system: A system that guides the cable carrier to prevent cable loops in the robot work area.
glossary.CMOS battery: A controller battery whose low state is indicated by an incorrect date and clock in the controller log.
glossary.continuity testing: A digital multimeter test performed on de-energized, isolated circuits that triggers an audible beep when component resistance drops below a threshold.
glossary.Dashboard Server: A remote control interface on Universal Robots controllers accessed over a TCP/IP socket on port 29999 using newline-terminated commands.
glossary.datafs: A storage partition on a UR controller SD card holding user programs, serial and log files, and controller calibration configuration files.
glossary.Dual Robot Calibration: A calibration routine that calibrates a robot across its full workspace so production can resume after joint replacement without modifying waypoints.
glossary.energy isolating device: A mechanical device capable of being locked out with a hasp, attachment point, or locking mechanism, excluding push buttons and control circuit devices.
glossary.fine calibration: A recalibration procedure used when external axes lack calibration values, but not when calibration values already exist.
glossary.flat ring: A joint seal that must be replaced on all robot joints if wear or damage is detected on any single ring.
glossary.flight record: A diagnostic tool that plots joint position, velocity, acceleration, motor current, and torque at the moment a fault occurs.
glossary.galvanic isolation: Electrical isolation established between circuits using an intermediate relay to mitigate noise interference from external equipment.
glossary.lockout/tagout: Procedures under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 to disable machinery and prevent the release of hazardous energy during servicing.
glossary.Lost Link Counter: A dedicated hardware register in an EtherCAT slave that increments whenever a physical communication link is interrupted.
glossary.magic files: Automated scripts on a USB stick that automatically back up robot programs, installation files, and configuration files.
glossary.predictive maintenance: Maintenance initiated based on predictions of failure made using observed data such as temperature, noise, and vibration.
glossary.preventive maintenance: Maintenance that is scheduled, timed, or based on an operating cycle.
glossary.Program Correction by Key Waypoints: A utility that adjusts fixed waypoints when transferring programs between robots or restoring program operation following joint replacements.
glossary.programState: A Dashboard Server query command that returns STOPPED if no program is running, PLAYING if running, or PAUSED if paused.
glossary.protective stop: A controller-initiated stop caused by proximity to a limit where the robot halts program execution while retaining electrical power.
glossary.pulse stretcher: An off-delay circuit in a high-speed sensor ensuring fast signals persist long enough for slower PLC scan cycles to detect them.
glossary.reactive maintenance: Maintenance done after equipment has failed or stopped.
glossary.revolution counter: An axis position counter updated against a synchronization position marking in an ABB robot controller.
glossary.robotmode: A Dashboard Server query command that returns controller power and brake states such as POWER_OFF, IDLE, or RUNNING.
glossary.Safety Control Board: A robot controller board whose diagnostic LEDs show normal communication with a slow green flash and hardware or safety errors with permanent red.
glossary.safetystatus: A Dashboard Server query command that returns the safety state such as NORMAL, PROTECTIVE_STOP, or FAULT.
glossary.stored energy: Potentially hazardous residual energy that must be relieved, disconnected, restrained, and rendered safe after applying lockout devices.
glossary.stress loop: An intentional cable loop built into an installation near a connector to prevent undue stress on the cable.
glossary.Support File: A diagnostic bundle automatically generated inside the robot controller that packages log files, robot programs, and flight reports.
glossary.torque wrench: A calibrated tool used during functional inspections to confirm that robot arm bolts and tooling fasteners are properly torqued.
glossary.TRIAC: A solid-state switching device whose high off-state leakage current exceeding 1 mA makes it unsuitable as an input for PLCs.
glossary.unlock protective stop: A Dashboard Server command that releases a protective stop, subject to an enforced 5-second delay under certain fault conditions.
glossary.Working Counter: An EtherCAT frame field that indicates slave communication failure and causes the master to discard input data when unexpected.
glossary.ESD vacuum: An electrostatic discharge vacuum cleaner used to clean accumulated dirt or dust inside the control box.

quiz.question: According to NIST manufacturing studies, how does the downtime of establishments relying most heavily on reactive maintenance compare to those relying on it least?
choices: They experience equal downtime but higher defect rates.
quiz.explanation: Manufacturing establishments relying most heavily on reactive maintenance experience 3.3 times more downtime than those relying on it least.

quiz.question: Why does Universal Robots prohibit the use of compressed air for cleaning a robot arm?
choices: It can strip exterior paint and markings.
It generates electrostatic charge on joint housings.
It increases air pressure inside sealed gearboxes.
quiz.explanation: Compressed air must never be used to clean the robot arm because it can damage internal components.

quiz.question: Under OSHA standard 29 CFR 1910.147, which devices are NOT considered energy isolating devices?
choices: Push buttons, selector switches, and control circuit devices
quiz.explanation: Push buttons, selector switches, and control circuit devices are not considered energy isolating devices under OSHA standards.

quiz.question: Which range of Universal Robots error codes designates faults occurring on e-Series and newer controllers?
quiz.explanation: Universal Robots error code numbers higher than 256 designate faults on e-Series and newer controllers, while codes 1 to 255 apply to CB3 and earlier controllers.

quiz.question: To what torque value must the screws securing the robot joint lids be tightened when using calibrated torque tools?
quiz.explanation: Screws securing the joint lids must be tightened to 0.4 Nm using calibrated torque tools.

quiz.question: How much mechanical motion does a properly engaged joint brake permit before hitting the brake pin?
quiz.explanation: A properly engaged joint brake permits only a limited mechanical motion of one to two degrees before hitting the brake pin.

quiz.question: Why are TRIAC output solid-state switches unsuitable as inputs for programmable logic controllers?
choices: Their off-state leakage current exceeds 1 mA
They only switch DC negative polarities
quiz.explanation: High off-state leakage current exceeding 1 mA makes TRIAC outputs unsuitable as inputs for programmable logic controllers.

quiz.question: In an EtherCAT network, what does an unexpected Working Counter value in a returned datagram frame indicate to the master?
choices: The network cycle time has decreased
A slave device has duplicated its node address
Slave communication failure has occurred, causing the master to discard input data
The physical cable length exceeds 100 meters
quiz.explanation: In EtherCAT networks, an unexpected Working Counter in a returned frame indicates slave communication failure and causes the master to discard input data.

quiz.question: What is the first step when updating revolution counters on an ABB robot system?
choices: Re-flash the controller operating system image
Move the robot and positioner axes to their respective zero positions at the synchronization marking
Replace the serial measurement board backup battery
Enter resolver calibration offset angles manually
quiz.explanation: The first step when updating the revolution counter is to move the robot and positioner axes to their respective zero positions at the synchronization marking.

quiz.question: Which type of Move node is NOT supported by the Universal Robots Program Correction by Key Waypoints utility?
choices: Move nodes configured with Use Joint Angles
quiz.explanation: Program Correction by Key Waypoints supports only fixed waypoints and does not support Move nodes configured with Use Joint Angles.

quiz.question: What does the robotmode state RUNNING indicate when queried from the Universal Robots Dashboard Server?
choices: A robot program is actively moving the manipulator arm
The robot is powered on with brakes released, distinct from program execution
The controller is currently undergoing a system backup
quiz.explanation: The robot mode state Running indicates that the robot is powered on with brakes released, which is distinct from program execution.

quiz.question: What specific condition triggers error 163 (TOO_FREQUENT_PROTECTIVE_STOPS) on a Universal Robots controller?
choices: More than 5 protective stops within 1 hour
More than 10 emergency stops within 24 hours
A joint encounters more than 50 protective stops within 8 hours
Controller CPU temperature exceeds 80 degrees Celsius
quiz.explanation: When a joint encounters more than 50 protective stops within 8 hours, error 163: TOO_FREQUENT_PROTECTIVE_STOPS is triggered and imposes a 5-second delay before unlock is permitted.
